long_biography.plain_text:
Ivan Meštrović portrayed Milica Banac repeatedly, beginning with a bronze bust made when she was 24 and returning to her likeness in a gilded profile relief. Their friendship continued in correspondence with the sculptor and his wife Olga. Works dedicated to Banac remained in her family collection, and later portraits preserved the bobbed hair and loose coats that became her signature style.

Banac moved through cultural and social circles in Zagreb, Dubrovnik, London, Paris and the Riviera. Her homes received figures including the Duke and Duchess of Kent, the Prince of Greece and Prince Rainier of Monaco. She settled permanently in Monaco and died there in 1970; several Meštrović portraits remained with her descendants.
